segments.text: Economics studies how scarce resources are allocated. Paper I builds the theoretical toolkit: how individuals and firms decide (microeconomics), how the economy as a whole behaves (macroeconomics), how money and banking work, how government taxing and spending affects the economy (fiscal policy), and how countries trade and develop. Paper II applies that same toolkit specifically to Pakistan. The single most useful habit across both papers is separating a movement along a curve (caused by a change in the variable on that curve’s own axis) from a shift of the whole curve (caused by a change in something else) - most exam confusion traces back to blurring this distinction.
